entries.name: East of Eden
entries.description: The new “East of Eden” adaptation is a family affair in more ways than one. Not only does the story focus on the tale of two troubled households, but it is also created and written by Zoe Kazan, granddaughter of Hollywood legend Elia Kazan, who directed the 1955 film version of the novel. This time around, the younger Kazan will tell a more complete version of Steinbeck’s generational epic that brings Florence Pugh’s Cathy to the center of the drama. With Christopher Abbott and Mike Faist stepping into the roles of the Trask brothers, this Netflix miniseries looks poised to be the next big binge watch. — Adrienne

entries.name: Verity
entries.description: They may be marketing this new Colleen Hoover adaptation as a “romantic thriller” but all signs point to Verity being a good, old-fashioned gothic horror story. We’ve got the innocent protagonist in Dakota Johnson, who plays a ghostwriter hired to finish the novel of a famous author left unconscious after a family tragedy. Then there’s Josh Hartnett, the conveniently handsome husband of the comatose Verity. Finally, we have Verity herself, played by Anne Hathaway, whose writings may hold the key to her mysterious injuries. Add in a remote lake house and you’ve got a recipe for a gothic melodrama fueled by obsession, lies, and devastating secrets. — Adrienne

entries.name: Digger
entries.description: Ready for one of the most divisive movies of the year — one that might become Tom Cruise’s modern-day Magnolia? This satire from filmmaker Alejandro G. Iñárritu, who has experienced popular and critical schisms before with both Babel and Bardo, situates Cruise as the most powerful man in the world, a man who essentially jumps up on Oprah’s couch to declare he’s going to save the world. — Arno

entries.name: Beware Boiúna
entries.description: Believe it or not, the world does need another movie about a giant killer snake, and Beware Boiúna is that movie. Like the best animal attack movies, Beware Boiúna invests in the human dynamics before it tears them apart, as a medical humanitarian team (featuring Happy Death Day’s Jessica Rothe and Fear Street’s Kiana Madeira) runs afoul of mercenaries (led by Logan Marshall-Green) exploiting the natural resources of the Amazon. Enter Boiúna, the giant snake spirit who takes her job of maintaining balance in the jungle seriously, and at the expense of these human intruders. — James

entries.name: Carrie
entries.description: Master of horror Mike Flanagan is bringing literature’s most telekinetic teen to the small screen this fall with an eight-episode series for Prime Video. Set in the modern day of cyberbullying and social media, “Carrie” stars Summer H. Howell (Curse of Chucky, Hunter Hunter) as the misunderstood misfit whose supernatural powers lead to tragedy. The king of Stephen King adaptations has previously delivered fairly faithful versions of Gerald’s Game, Doctor Sleep, and The Life of Chuck, but with “Carrie” Flanagan seems to be taking more liberties with his source material. As the director told Deadline, “'Carrie' was written half a century ago. 'Carrie' was adapted spectacularly by Brian De Palma. It is iconic. It is untouchable. However, the world has changed quite a lot.” Long-time Flanagan collaborator Samantha Sloyan co-stars as Carrie White's mother Margaret, alongside Matthew Lillard, Amber Midthunder, and an ensemble of up-and-coming talent. -- Adrienne

entries.name: Below
entries.description: Take a spooky vacation this fall to Newfoundland, Canada to see how Josh Hartnett's accent holds up as he navigates a horror-thriller that supports the YouTube conspiracy theories about alien life forms living beneath the water's surface of our world. The island town folk horror craze in our post-“Widow’s Bay” culture is quite welcome, especially in limited series form that employs Charlie Heaton, Mackenzie David, and Natasha Henstridge, even! — Arno

entries.name: Animals
entries.description: Ben Affleck directs and stars in this political thriller from Netflix, in which he plays a Los Angeles mayoral candidate whose son is kidnapped, putting him and his wife (Kerry Washington) in a situation where coming up with the ransom money means exposing dark secrets from their past. Affleck originally envisioned Matt Damon starring opposite the director’s ex-wife Jennifer Garner, but Damon’s schedule wouldn’t allow it due to filming a little arthouse flick known as Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey. — James

entries.name: The Social Reckoning
entries.description: When The Social Network premiered 16 years ago, Instagram still had a month before launch, Twitter had grown by 100 million users, and Facebook was four years into using their new algorithmic news feed, which prioritized delivering users the most “relevant” content. A lot has changed since then, and writer-director Aaron Sorkin is back to explore social media’s toxic evolution with The Social Reckoning. Starring Mikey Madison, Jeremy Allen White, and Jeremy Strong as Mark Zuckerberg, the sequel will unspool the 2021 Facebook whistleblower leak that confirmed Facebook was well aware of the harm they were causing and had no intention of stopping. Keep an ear out for what’s not said in this continuing saga, as Sorkin has revealed the legal restrictions on his work were not insignificant. As he said to The New York Times, ”The irony wasn’t lost on anybody that we were doing a thorough fact check of a movie about a company unwilling to do the same thing.” — Adrienne

entries.name: Other Mommy
entries.description: Do you remember the trailer for Smile, when that woman was standing next to the car and suddenly her head just dropped into frame like it was dangling from her neck? That’s totally the jump scare-filled vibe we’re getting as Jessica Chastain and director Rob Savage work through some mommy issues as eight-year-old Bela (Arabella Olivia Clark) watches the disintegration of her parents’ marriage while contending with the scary “other mommy” who lives in her closet. Savage is the filmmaker who brought us the pandemic-era Zoom nightmare “Host," so don't be surprised when this becomes a hit. — James

entries.name: Fjord
entries.description: “It is impossible to know what happens inside a family’s private life.” In acclaimed writer-director Cristian Mungiu’s Fjord, inspired by true events, Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve bring depth and nuance to their roles as a Romanian-Norwegian couple fighting to regain custody of their children after allegations of physical abuse. Restrained, affecting, and exceptionally well-written, the Palme d’Or–winning drama gradually unpacks a conflict shaped by parenting, faith, cultural identity, and the role of the state. Refusing easy answers or simple judgments, Fjord is a tense and thought-provoking film sure to spark conversation. — Matt

entries.name: V/H/S/Mixtape
entries.description: If one thing’s for certain, horror fans love an anthology film, and the V/H/S franchise has been delivering found footage frights in that format since 2012. Since then, the series has gone viral, taken us back to the ‘80s, ‘90s, and beyond, and celebrated the spookiest night of the year. Now, they’re exploring the malicious side of the melodic with four horror shorts from directors like Ernest Dickerson, David Moreau, and Renee Zhan, as well as musicians RZA, Tobias Forge, and featuring Jim Henson’s Creature Shop alongside legendary metal monsters, GWAR. Now that’s a line-up I’d happily play on repeat. — Adrienne

entries.name: VisionQuest
entries.description: The trilogy that started with "WandaVision" and continued with "Agatha All Along" ends with "VisionQuest," where we finally find out what Vision has been up to since turning white and flying off years ago. Expect a roster of familiar faces filling up Vision's mind palace, including James Spader as Ultron, James D'Arcy as J.A.R.V.I.S. (who we last saw in "Agent Carter"), and deep-cut Faran Tahir as Raza, the leader of the Ten Rings faction that kidnapped Tony Stark way back in Iron Man. We can't wait to see how these threads weave together. — Vanessa

entries.name: Crystal Lake
entries.description: Fans familiar with the horrors of Camp Crystal Lake know it all started with a tragedy. And this October, we’ll get to witness the fallout from those events in the new series “Crystal Lake.” Linda Cardellini stars as Pamela Voorhees in the eight-episode season that follows the mourning mother with murderous intentions. But as we all know, it’s not just Pam the residents of this doomed town need to fear. There’s something in the woods around Crystal Lake, and “all it knows how to do is kill.” — Adrienne

entries.name: Street Fighter
entries.description: Call us crazy, but the third big screen adaptation of the classic arcade fighting game could be a charm in this bumpy film franchise. Noah Centineo (To All the Boys I’ve Loved Before) and Andrew Koji (“Warrior”) star as fighting duo Ken and Ryu, who reunite to compete in the World Warrior Tournament, battling such foes as franchise faves Blanka (Jason Momoa), Chun-Li (Callina Liang), M. Bison (David Dastmalchian), not to mention the inspired casting of singer Orville Peck as Vega. The trailer gives us hope that Street Fighter captures that feeling of mashing buttons on your controller.  — James

entries.name: You Can See Everything
entries.description: The internet lost its mind when Nathan Fielder dropped a teaser no one expected for a new documentary no one knew was coming at the Telluride Film Festival. The writer-director has made a name for himself with his peculiar blend of comedy and reality TV that often results in a surrealist examination of the human condition. Expect nothing less from You Can See Everything. Apparently while none of us were looking, Fielder and his crew moved in with Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes to capture her last month of freedom before beginning her 11-year prison sentence for defrauding investors. The result appears to be a multi-year odyssey that A24 is calling “a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss.” — Adrienne

entries.name: Sacrifice
entries.description: French filmmaker Romain Gavras has always been a full volume provocateur, and he's going for it again with Sacrifice, his first film in English and his second Netflix movie (after Athena). Chris Evans plays a disgraced movie star mounting a comeback by attending a charitable gala in this thriller that also introduces Anya Taylor-Joy as the head of a radical activist group who believe they can save the world from environmental collapse if they — insert movie title here — three people on this given occasion. — Arno

entries.name: The Terminal List
entries.detail: Season 2 premieres October 21 on Prime Video
entries.description: It’s been four long years since “The Terminal List” first premiered, so here’s all the things you need to know about Season 2. Now a wanted fugitive after completing his revenge campaign, Reece (Chris Pratt) is offered a presidential pardon for “one last mission.” He’s guided by Gabriel Luna, who joins the cast as a former SEAL/CIA operative, as they attempt to take down a former Iraqi commando who may be the key to a larger geopolitical conspiracy. — James

entries.name: Clayface
entries.description: You’re probably already well-aware of the latest Gotham rogues gallery film from producer Matt Reeves (The Batman). But did you know the script was written by Mike Flanagan? And were you aware it’s directed by James Watkins, the man responsible for such nightmares as Eden Lake, Speak No Evil, and one of the most messed up “Black Mirror” episodes of all time? Given all that, I think we might need to head to the theater to see the tragic tale of actor Matt Hagen, whose pursuit of physical perfection leads him to an experimental procedure that will cost him everything. — Adrienne

entries.name: Klara and the Sun
entries.description: Jenna Ortega stars as Klara, the “Artificial Friend” assigned to bond with a sick 14-year-old girl named Josie (Mia Tharia) in this big screen adaptation of Kazuo Ishiguro’s dystopian novel. Taika Waititi returns to the director’s chair after 2023’s First Goal Wins, and the ensemble cast includes Amy Adams as Josie’s mother, Natasha Lyonne, Steve Buscemi, and Aran (son of Cillian) Murphy. -- James

entries.name: Wicker
entries.description: Alexander Skarsgård’s hotness is not restricted to human form. In what might be our most anticipated indie movie of the year, the Skars plays a man who is brought to life by his village’s basketmaker (Peter Dinklage), who weaves him together from wood and other natural materials. His sole purpose is to bring happiness and carnal pleasure to Olivia Colman’s character, a fisherwoman who has been ridiculed and ostracized from her rigid 17th-century coastal village community. What a reason to live any sort of life. The movie feels like a shot across the bow of the AI era, making its eccentricities that much more appealing. — Arno

plot_text.plain_text: In the farmlands of the Salinas Valley in California, successive generations of two families, the Trasks and the Hamiltons, are destined to reenact the fateful story of Cain and Abel.

plot_text.plain_text: The most powerful man in the world embarks on a frantic mission to prove he is humanity's savior before the disaster he's unleashed destroys everything.

A team of doctors embark on a local mission in the Amazon rain forest, but it soon becomes clear that not everybody - or everything - is happy to see them. Their sudden appearance draws the attention of an animal predator, the "Boiúna."
A sheltered girl with telekinetic powers is bullied, leading to a horrific, bloody incident due to her domineering mother's influence.
When a mysterious sea creature terrorizes a remote town, a fisherman must fight to protect his family, his community, and his way of life.
Desperate to pay their son's ransom, a mayoral candidate and his wife resort to extreme measures, revealing dark secrets they never intended to bring to light.

plot_text.plain_text: Follows Frances Haugen, a young Facebook engineer, who enlisted the help of Jeff Horwitz, a Wall Street Journal reporter, to blow the whistle on the social network's most guarded secrets.

Bela, an 8-year-old girl living in a home with marital problems, confronts a sinister entity which comes out of her closet. The presence, whom she calls "Other Mommy," becomes increasingly threatening to her and her family.
An immigrant Romanian family living in Norway is subject to an investigation and faces the scrutiny of the local judicial system.
It presents a new anthology in which music and sound become a source of terror.
Vision is faced with many challenges while trying to regain his memory and humanity.
Prequel series to Friday the 13th, follows a doomed small town where camp counselors come to die.

plot_text.plain_text: Street Fighters Ryu and Ken reunite when Chun-Li recruits them for the World Warrior Tournament. As they face a hidden conspiracy, they must confront each other and their past-or face destruction.

Thirty-four days before she's sent to prison, notorious Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait becomes a mind-bending three-year journey.
At an elite fundraising gala, celebrities and socialites find themselves in danger when armed activists storm the venue in pursuit of a legendary relic that could unlock supernatural powers.
A former Navy SEAL officer investigates why his entire platoon was ambushed during a high-stakes covert mission.
Rising Hollywood star Matt Hagen descends into a horrifying revenge-filled monster when scientific ambition strips him of his identity and humanity.
A robot girl designed to prevent loneliness tries to save a heartbroken family of humans.

An ostracized fisherwoman commissions the local basketmaker to weave her a husband, but when her wicker creation proves unexpectedly extraordinary, his presence ignites jealousy and upheaval that threatens their quiet village.
